trust_decision.summary: Whoever knows only a public hash must not learn its delete code / uploader data (API::info returns the whole meta.json), and a delete must only succeed with the stored code or a non-empty master code/IP (checked separately in API::delete and in the architect URL router).

landing_point.why: The summary names the info API; API::info returns getMetadataOfHash() verbatim, which contains delete_code, delete_url, ip, useragent (written at src/inc/api.class.php:182-195).

fix_sites.module_kind: API handler (allowlist of returned meta fields)
API handler (delete-code check switched to shared helper)

fix_sites.entry_point: any public URL containing a delete_<code> segment, routed by architect() (web/index.php:50)
fix_sites.module_kind: front router / second implementation of the delete check (loose == comparison, empty MASTER_DELETE_IP)

fix_sites.entry_point: upload (/api/upload, MCP upload_*) and album creation, which mint delete codes via getRandomString (src/inc/api.class.php:181, src/inc/api.class.php:302)
new shared helper isValidDeleteCode used by both delete routes (fix.diff:61-76)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/inc/core.php:276-292 (architect() URL delete check, separate from API::delete in src/inc/api.class.php:237-257); also credential producer getRandomString at src/inc/core.php:551-559

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the JSON info API leaking metadata; the delete_<code> URL router in core.php and the random-string helper look like unrelated legacy UI routing and a generic utility, and API::delete already rejects empty codes via `!$code` (src/inc/api.class.php:243).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Info must keep returning public metadata (hash, mime, size, sha1, uploaded; album 'hashes'/'type'/'created'), upload/album responses must still hand the delete_code to the uploader, and deletion with the correct code or a configured MASTER_DELETE_CODE must keep working; a denylist or stripping delete_code from meta/upload response breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: file meta.json vs album meta.json (different key sets: hashes/type/created vs mime/size/sha1) (src/inc/api.class.php:182-195, src/inc/api.class.php:296-304)
meta fields added later by the flushviews cron (views, last_accessed) (src/inc/core.php:1414)
hash with no stored delete_code (getDeleteCodeOfHash returns false) vs empty code '' via /delete_/<hash> (src/inc/core.php:959-966, src/inc/core.php:280-282)
falsy numeric code '0' under loose == against false (src/inc/core.php:282; fix.diff:198-208)
MASTER_DELETE_CODE defined as '' (docker default) vs undefined (docker/rootfs/start.sh:32)

O7_producer.where: meta.json is produced by API::handleFile (src/inc/api.class.php:182-199), API::createAlbum (src/inc/api.class.php:296-306), flushViews cron merge (src/inc/core.php:1414) and admin rebuildMeta (src/inc/core.php:1629-1643), all merged via updateMetaData (src/inc/core.php:1442-1453)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: URL delete route still authorises any request whose getUserIP() equals MASTER_DELETE_IP, and getUserIP() trusts client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For / Client-IP headers, so the master-IP branch into deleteHash is not tied to the real peer; fix only added a non-empty check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: IP trust looks like a reverse-proxy/deployment concern and MASTER_DELETE_IP is an opt-in admin feature, not the delete-code leak the report describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the router fix site but a different function (src/inc/core.php:573-599); one file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: album page passes each member's full meta (or original_filename) into the template / a JSON album view
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the controller already loads full $hmeta per item; a maintainer adding captions or filenames would forward it wholesale

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a separate MCP tool (e.g. list/album info) calling getMetadataOfHash directly instead of API::info
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the MCP class claims to delegate to API but already contains its own logic (transform_image, src/inc/mcp.class.php:94-135), so a direct metadata read is plausible

O8b_injection_room.sibling: storageControllerUpload also pushing meta.json to S3/FTP/alt-folder, which may be publicly readable
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer syncing state across scaled nodes would want meta.json replicated alongside the file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: duplicate-upload shortcut returning the existing hash's delete_code/delete_url
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the legacy endpoint src/api/upload.php:80-84 already attaches getDeleteCodeOfHash() to the response; porting that convenience to the dedup branch is natural

O9_family: credential disclosure and weak credential check (CWE-522): delete code exposed via metadata API, loose/empty-code comparison, predictable code generation

services: file/ffmpeg binaries for some content types

Hosted HTML pages run same-origin script (src/content-controllers/html/html.controller.php) and could call /api/info; separate feature.
unverified: Repo size not measured (no shell); likely small (~75 PHP files) and may trip tiny_repo (<5 MB) - check before selection.
O8 route concerns delete authorisation via spoofable client-IP headers; whether the advisory's property is read to cover MASTER_DELETE_IP is a judgement call.
Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest is unknown for all O8 routes.
Whether a stored, already-predictable delete code (rand()) needs regeneration for existing uploads was not assessed.
